blurb: Toy breed born either hairless with a silky crest or fully coated as a powderpuff
description: The Chinese Crested Dog is a small, fine-boned toy breed in hairless and powderpuff varieties, with large erect ears, little shedding and a playful air.
answer: The Chinese Crested Dog is a small, fine-boned toy breed that comes in two varieties, the hairless and the coated powderpuff, which can appear in the same litter. It stands about 23 to 33 cm tall and typically weighs 4.5 to 5.9 kg; despite its name, its origins are more likely in Mexico or Africa than in China.

body: Hairless dogs have been found in many parts of the world, and because the Chinese Crested shares its hairless mutation with the Xoloitzcuintli, the modern breed is thought to have originated in Africa or, more likely, Mexico. Spanish explorers recorded such dogs in Central and South America in the 1500s.

In the 1950s Debora Wood founded the Crest Haven kennel, which absorbed the dogs of burlesque dancer Gypsy Rose Lee; these two lines are the foundation of the modern breed. The FCI recognised the breed in 1987, with China listed as its country of origin, and the American Kennel Club in 1991.

The breed is fine-boned, with almond-shaped eyes, large erect ears and hare feet with elongated toes. There is no colour standard. The hairless has soft, humanlike skin with hair on the head (crest), feet (socks) and tail (plume), and the amount of body hair varies widely. The powderpuff has a long, soft double coat. All hairless dogs carry one copy of the hairless gene, which is lethal before birth when inherited twice.

The breed is commonly described as loving, playful and entertaining, intelligent and suited to obedience sports. It is said to be relatively sensitive and to do best with consistent, gentle training. Powderpuffs are noted for learning tricks readily.

Cresteds enjoy daily outdoor exercise but are not a high-energy breed. The powderpuff needs frequent brushing to prevent matting, and many owners keep it in a pony cut. The hairless variety's skin can be prone to acne, dryness and sunburn, especially in light-skinned dogs. Nails need careful trimming because the quick runs deep. Shedding is described as little to none.

One 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.4 years. Conditions reported in the breed include poor dentition in hairless dogs, primary lens luxation, at least two forms of progressive retinal atrophy, dry eye syndrome, canine multiple system degeneration and patellar luxation. Genetic tests exist for primary lens luxation and one form of progressive retinal atrophy.

faq.a: The breed is described as having little to no shedding. The powderpuff still needs regular brushing, and the hairless needs skin care.

faq.q: How long do Chinese Crested Dogs live?
faq.a: One 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.4 years, above the average for purebred dogs.

faq.q: Is the Chinese Crested Dog really from China?
faq.a: Probably not. Because it shares its hairless mutation with the Xoloitzcuintli, its origins are thought to be in Mexico or Africa, although the FCI lists China as the country of origin.
